decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Mega Gengar. Aerodactyl + Dragonite lead provides immediate turn-one strength: Dragonite's Inner Focus immune-bypasses Raichu Fake Out while threatening 4x super-effective damage on Garchomp/Charizard with Ice Spinner and Rock Slide. Aerodactyl deters Choice Scarf Garchomp Rock Slide and Charizard Heat Wave with Wide Guard or sets Tailwind. Mega Gengar traps key targets like Primarina and Venusaur in the back, while Arcanine provides Intimidate and Snarl/Will-O-Wisp mitigation.
decisions.notebook: Matchup strategy: Aerodactyl + Dragonite lead counters Raichu Fake Out and Zard-Y/Garchomp spread moves with Wide Guard/Inner Focus. Mega Gengar in back traps and neutralizes Grass/Fairy threats like Venusaur/Primarina.

decisions.rationale: Intend Mega Charizard Y. Lead Scarf Garchomp + Raichu aims to deny Aerodactyl’s Tailwind with Fake Out while Garchomp immediately threatens Mega Gengar. Primarina is the protected Dragonite, Krookodile, and Arcanine answer; Charizard supplies the sun endgame once Rock Slide pressure is managed.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Mega Gengar Shadow Tag, Focus Sash Aerodactyl with Tailwind/Wide Guard, Life Orb Dragonite, Intimidate Arcanine and Scarf Intimidate Krookodile. Preserve Primarina for Dragonite/Krookodile/Arcanine. Scarf Garchomp is the key immediate speed piece versus Mega Gengar and Aerodactyl; deny Tailwind where possible. Mega Charizard Y should not be exposed to Aerodactyl or Dragonite Rock Slide without positioning.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Dragonite)
decisions.rationale: Scarf Garchomp outspeeds our entire team and threatens a high-damage Dragon Claw or spread Rock Slide. At 200 Speed, Aerodactyl's +3 priority Wide Guard executes before Raichu's +3 Fake Out (max 178 Speed). Combining Wide Guard with Dragonite's Protect completely blocks all potential attacks while safely revealing Garchomp's Choice lock for Turn 2. Wide Guard can also be used consecutively in Gen 9 if Garchomp locks into Rock Slide.

Dragon Claw cleanly removes Dragonite before its 4x-effective Ice Spinner and cannot be stopped by Wide Guard. Nuzzle gives the best chance to deny or cripple Tailwind while preserving Raichu; Garchomp is guaranteed faster than Dragonite.

Garchomp is Choice-locked into Dragon Claw from turn 1. A double switch to Arcanine and Gengar absorbs all incoming attacks with minimal damage: Intimidate weakens Garchomp's Dragon Claw onto Arcanine, while Gengar safely resists Raichu's Electric attacks. This positions Mega Gengar on turn 3 to trap both foes with Shadow Tag while preserving full team health.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp Choice Scarf locked into Dragon Claw. Raichu Lum Berry.

decisions.rationale: Raichu guarantees the immediate Aerodactyl KO before it can Tailwind or use Wide Guard again. Garchomp is locked but moves before Dragonite and pressures its Protect; even if Dragonite survives and KOs Garchomp with Ice Spinner, removing Aerodactyl cleanly preserves Primarina and Charizard positioning for the endgame.

Garchomp is Scarfed and locked into Dragon Claw; without Protect, Gengar dies to Dragon Claw. Mega Evolving on Protect activates Shadow Tag, trapping both foes. Raichu's Thunderbolt is disabled by Cursed Body. Arcanine easily survives -1 Dragon Claw (Sitrus Berry triggers if needed) and can burn Garchomp with Will-O-Wisp to permanently neutralize its physical attack output while trapped.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp Choice Scarf locked into Dragon Claw. Raichu Lum Berry (Thunderbolt disabled turn 2 by Cursed Body).

decisions.rationale: Scarf Garchomp guarantees Dragon Claw before even Mega Gengar and KOs from its shown range if it does not Protect. Raichu Protect blocks Arcanine’s priority ExtremeSpeed and avoids Gengar’s Sludge Bomb, preserving it while forcing Gengar’s Protect or removal.
decisions.notebook: Opponent may use Mega Gengar Shadow Tag to punish passive positioning; prioritize immediate Scarf Garchomp pressure into it. Preserve Primarina for Dragonite, Krookodile, and Arcanine. Avoid exposing Mega Charizard Y to Aerodactyl or Dragonite Rock Slide without safe positioning.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is burned and at -1 Atk, so Choice Scarf Dragon Claw deals only ~15-26% to Gengar-Mega (at 42% HP), allowing Gengar to comfortably survive. Gengar (200 Speed) outspeeds Raichu (143-178 Speed) and hits it with Sludge Bomb (47-109% damage) before Raichu can Nuzzle. Double-targeting Raichu with Sludge Bomb and Flare Blitz guarantees the KO on Raichu while Shadow Tag prevents switches.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp Choice Scarf locked into Dragon Claw. Raichu Lum Berry; Thunderbolt disabled by Cursed Body on T2.

decisions.rationale: Scarf Garchomp is guaranteed faster than Mega Gengar and Dragon Claw KOs from its shown HP if it does not Protect. Nuzzle Arcanine gains valuable paralysis while preserving Primarina for Dragonite and Arcanine; Raichu is less essential after Gengar falls. A second Gengar Protect is the main downside, but abandoning the immediate KO risks Shadow Ball pressure.
decisions.notebook: Opponent revealed Mega Gengar with Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect; it may use repeat Protect under pressure. Arcanine revealed Intimidate, Will-O-Wisp, and likely physical priority via ExtremeSpeed. Preserve Primarina as the primary Dragonite/Arcanine answer. Avoid exposing Mega Charizard Y while Aerodactyl or Dragonite can threaten with Rock Slide. Scarf Garchomp outspeeds Mega Gengar and should maintain immediate Dragon Claw pressure when legal.

decisions.rationale: Switch Charizard in: Garchomp’s locked Dragon Claw still forces Gengar to respect the KO, while Charizard avoids Primarina entering directly into a possible Sludge Bomb. Preserve Primarina for Dragonite and Arcanine; do not Mega Charizard until Rock Slide users are better controlled.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Mega Gengar has Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect; expect Protect when threatened by Scarf Garchomp. Arcanine has Intimidate, Will-O-Wisp, Flare Blitz, and likely ExtremeSpeed/Snarl utility. Aerodactyl has Wide Guard, Tailwind, Taunt, Rock Slide and Focus Sash; it and Dragonite’s Rock Slide make early Mega Charizard Y risky. Preserve Primarina as the key answer to Dragonite and Arcanine. Scarf Garchomp outspeeds Mega Gengar and keeps immediate Dragon Claw pressure when legal.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is Scarfed and outspeeds Gengar (200 Spe vs 201-253 Spe). Protect keeps Gengar safe from fast Dragon Claw or Charizard attacks while maintaining Shadow Tag trap. Arcanine uses Snarl to lower Charizard's Special Attack by 1 stage; because Shadow Tag is active, Charizard cannot switch out to clear the SpA drop.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp Choice Scarf locked into Dragon Claw (-1 Atk, burned). Raichu fainted; Lum Berry was consumed earlier. Charizard mega Y Drought set Sun T5.

decisions.rationale: Dragon Claw forces Mega Gengar to Protect or be removed before it moves. Air Slash pressures Arcanine substantially more than its resisted Heat Wave and can deny its action with flinch; it also remains useful if Arcanine switches. Do not Mega yet: Drought is unnecessary for this line and Mega Charizard remains vulnerable to the opponent’s revealed Rock Slide users.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has shown a conservative Mega Gengar Protect pattern when directly threatened by Scarf Garchomp. Aerodactyl carries Focus Sash, Wide Guard, Tailwind, Taunt, and Rock Slide; Dragonite has Protect, ExtremeSpeed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, and Life Orb. Preserve Primarina as the main late-game answer into Dragonite and Arcanine. Avoid committing Mega Charizard Y into known Rock Slide pressure unless Drought’s immediate payoff is decisive.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp moves first with Choice Scarf and threatens to finish off Gengar-Mega (21% HP) with Dragon Claw. Switching Gengar-Mega to Dragonite safely absorbs Dragon Claw thanks to Garchomp's burn and -1 Attack drop. Arcanine using Snarl drops Charizard to -2 Special Attack, effectively neutering its offensive output while Dragonite threatens an immediate Ice Spinner KO on Garchomp next turn.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp Choice Scarf locked into Dragon Claw (-1 Atk, burned). Raichu fainted. Charizard Mega Y set Sun T5 (-1 SpA).

decisions.rationale: Scarf Garchomp threatens to remove Gengar before it can use a normal-priority attack; its consecutive Protect is reduced. Air Slash is the only listed Charizard attack that is not resisted by Arcanine and pressures its remaining health while avoiding Mega Charizard Y's Rock weakness. This maximizes the chance to clear both current foes for Primarina’s Dragonite endgame.

Dragonite's 4x super-effective Ice Spinner guarantees a KO on Garchomp (67% HP) even after taking a weak -1 burned Dragon Claw (~25-34%). Arcanine uses Snarl to further reduce Charizard's Special Attack to -2, neutering its remaining damage output for the endgame.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp Choice Scarf, Charizard Mega Y. Raichu fainted.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is unlikely to survive Dragonite’s 4x Ice Spinner, while a double target is vulnerable to Protect and may not cleanly KO through its remaining health. Preserve Primarina, the key Dragonite/Arcanine endgame piece, and deny this turn’s Rock Slide or Snarl pressure with Protect. Charizard can be traded later if needed for Primarina to finish.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Mega Gengar has repeatedly Protected when directly threatened by Scarf Garchomp. Aerodactyl revealed Focus Sash, Wide Guard, Tailwind, Taunt, Rock Slide, and Unnerve. Dragonite revealed Protect, ExtremeSpeed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, Life Orb, and Inner Focus. Arcanine revealed Intimidate, Flare Blitz, ExtremeSpeed, Will-O-Wisp, Snarl, and Sitrus Berry. Preserve Primarina as the primary late-game answer to Dragonite and Arcanine; avoid Mega Charizard Y into active Rock Slide pressure unless its immediate damage is decisive.

decisions.rationale: Dragonite (Speed 132) outspeeds Primarina (max Speed 112) and cannot be flinched due to Inner Focus. Arcanine's priority +2 Extreme Speed chips Charizard into guaranteed KO range for Dragonite's 4x super-effective Rock Slide before Primarina can attack. Eliminating Charizard secures a dominant endgame with Aerodactyl and Mega Gengar remaining.

Gengar-Mega brings clean 200 Speed outspeeding both active foes (Charizard 132-167, Primarina 80-112), traps them with Shadow Tag, and threatens an immediate Sludge Bomb KO on the 33% Primarina next turn. Aerodactyl is paralyzed at 81% HP (effective Speed 100) and cannot act before Charizard.

Ice Beam guarantees Dragonite’s KO if it does not Protect, while faster Air Slash guarantees Arcanine’s KO before its regular moves. Dragonite’s priority ExtremeSpeed cannot stop Charizard’s KO on Arcanine, and if Dragonite Protects, removing Arcanine still leaves a favorable 2v1. Do not Mega into potential Rock Slide.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Mega Gengar repeatedly Protected when directly threatened by Scarf Garchomp. Aerodactyl revealed Focus Sash, Wide Guard, Tailwind, Taunt, Rock Slide, and Unnerve. Dragonite revealed Protect, ExtremeSpeed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, Life Orb, and Inner Focus. Arcanine revealed Intimidate, Flare Blitz, ExtremeSpeed, Will-O-Wisp, Snarl, and Sitrus Berry. Preserve Primarina as the primary late-game answer to Dragonite and Arcanine; avoid Mega Charizard Y into active Rock Slide pressure unless immediate damage is decisive.

decisions.rationale: At +2 priority, Dragonite's Extreme Speed moves before both foes and finishes Primarina (33% HP). Gengar-Mega outspeeds Charizard (200 raw Speed) and hits it with Sludge Bomb (45.4-83.0%), with a high chance to KO Charizard from 60% HP on the same turn. Even if Charizard survives, both of the opponent's active threats are neutralized or severely weakened, leaving burned Scarf Garchomp unable to win.

Protect prevents Dragonite’s guaranteed ExtremeSpeed KO and Gengar’s Sludge Bomb. Charizard’s Air Slash is the immediate way to remove Dragonite before it can use its 4x-effective Rock Slide; Charizard is faster than Dragonite. Do not Mega Evolve: preserving 167 Speed is important versus Mega Gengar’s 165–200 range.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Dragonite's Life Orb Extreme Speed at +2 priority moves before Scarf Garchomp and Primarina, KOing the 33% Primarina before it can attack (34%+ damage). Gengar-Mega uses Protect to safely block Scarf Garchomp's attack. This leaves burned Garchomp alone against Dragonite and Gengar next turn.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Primarina must attempt the reduced-success Protect to deny the immediate double-up. Dragon Claw leaves Dragonite low enough for Garchomp to finish next turn if Protect succeeds; removing Gengar first instead leaves Dragonite able to Extreme Speed Primarina before it can KO it. This is the best available high-variance survival line.

Garchomp is Choice-locked into Dragon Claw and burned at 61% HP. Scarf Garchomp outspeeds both active Pokémon. Burned Dragon Claw deals ~26-37% to Aerodactyl, leaving Aerodactyl well above KO range. If Garchomp attacks Gengar-Mega, Gengar faints but Aerodactyl easily cleans up Garchomp with Rock Slide and burn ticks over 2 turns. If Garchomp attacks Aerodactyl, Gengar-Mega's Shadow Ball combined with Rock Slide and burn will finish Garchomp this turn.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp Choice Scarf, Charizard Mega Y.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is Choice-locked, and Dragon Claw into Gengar-Mega is the only route to immediately remove its 21% HP. A repeat Protect is reduced after last turn; Aerodactyl's Rock Slide is resisted and its paralysis leaves it slower. Targeting Aerodactyl permits Gengar to attack freely.

Garchomp is Choice-locked into Dragon Claw and burned, dealing only 26-37% per hit to Aerodactyl (at 81% HP). Aerodactyl easily survives two hits. Rock Slide is Aerodactyl's only attack, dealing direct damage to accelerate the KO alongside end-of-turn burn chip.
Garchomp is Choice-locked into Dragon Claw. Target Aerodactyl for the only available damaging action; the empty foe slot cannot advance the endgame.

Garchomp is Choice-locked into Dragon Claw and burned. Burned Dragon Claw deals 26.1–37.1% to Aerodactyl (currently at 49% HP), guaranteeing Aerodactyl survives this turn. Rock Slide deals 10.2–19.1% to Garchomp (at 12% HP), which combined with the end-of-turn burn tick guarantees the game-winning KO.
decisions.notebook:
Opponent sets revealed in Game 1:
- Charizard: Charizardite Y, Timid, Heat Wave / Solar Beam / Air Slash / Protect
- Garchomp: Choice Scarf, Jolly, Dragon Claw / Stomping Tantrum / Rock Slide / Poison Jab
- Primarina: Life Orb, Modest, Moonblast / Hydro Pump / Ice Beam / Protect
- Raichu: Lum Berry, Timid, Fake Out / Nuzzle / Thunderbolt / Protect
- Venusaur & Goodra-Hisui were benched.

decisions.rationale: Choice-Scarf Garchomp moves before the paralyzed Aerodactyl and Dragon Claw is neutral with a guaranteed KO from its shown HP. Rock Slide, Tailwind, and Wide Guard do not prevent this single-target KO.

Scarf Garchomp outspeeds paralyzed Aerodactyl and is locked into Dragon Claw. Aerodactyl cannot survive a hit at 18% HP, but Rock Slide is our only attacking move to KO Garchomp at 7% HP if Dragon Claw somehow fails to connect.
decisions.notebook:
Opponent sets revealed in Game 1:
- Charizard: Charizardite Y, Timid, Heat Wave / Solar Beam / Air Slash / Protect
- Garchomp: Choice Scarf, Jolly, Dragon Claw / Stomping Tantrum / Rock Slide / Poison Jab
- Primarina: Life Orb, Modest, Moonblast / Hydro Pump / Ice Beam / Protect
- Raichu: Lum Berry, Timid, Fake Out / Nuzzle / Thunderbolt / Protect
- Venusaur & Goodra-Hisui benched.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is Choice-locked and moves first even through Aerodactyl's paralysis. Dragon Claw is the only meaningful legal attack and should finish its remaining HP before it can Rock Slide; Wide Guard does not stop Dragon Claw.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Mega Gengar repeatedly Protected when directly threatened by Scarf Garchomp. Aerodactyl revealed Focus Sash, Wide Guard, Tailwind, Taunt, Rock Slide, Unnerve, and paralysis. Dragonite revealed Protect, ExtremeSpeed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, Life Orb, and Inner Focus. Arcanine revealed Intimidate, Flare Blitz, ExtremeSpeed, Will-O-Wisp, Snarl, and Sitrus Berry. Preserve Primarina as the primary late-game answer to Dragonite and Arcanine; avoid Mega Charizard Y into active Rock Slide pressure unless immediate damage is decisive.

reflections.summary: Mega Gengar was vulnerable to Choice Scarf Garchomp's speed advantage, allowing Garchomp to clean up Gengar and the rest of the chipped team without speed control active.
reflections.adjustment: Prioritize setting up Tailwind early with Aerodactyl to ensure Dragonite (with Ice Spinner) and Mega Gengar can outspeed and remove Choice Scarf Garchomp before it can sweep.
reflections.notebook:
Opponent sets revealed:
- Charizard: Charizardite Y, Timid (Heat Wave / Solar Beam / Air Slash / Protect)
- Garchomp: Choice Scarf, Jolly (Dragon Claw / Stomping Tantrum / Rock Slide / Poison Jab)
- Primarina: Life Orb, Modest (Moonblast / Hydro Pump / Ice Beam / Protect)
- Raichu: Lum Berry, Timid (Fake Out / Nuzzle / Thunderbolt / Protect)
- Venusaur & Goodra-Hisui: benched

Strategic notes:
- Opponent utilizes Choice Scarf Garchomp as an endgame clean-up sweeper.
- Tailwind is mandatory to reverse Garchomp's Scarf speed advantage and allow Ice Spinner Dragonite or Gengar to KO it.

reflections.summary: Won narrowly because Scarf Garchomp cleaned Mega Gengar, Dragonite, and Aerodactyl; however, the line depended on the critical Air Slash KO on Arcanine and Aerodactyl’s paralysis. The four were workable, but Mega Charizard Y was a risky preview choice into two Rock Slide users.
reflections.adjustment: Prioritize Raichu pressure on Aerodactyl with Fake Out/Nuzzle and preserve Charizard from Rock Slide turns; only commit the Charizard Mega plan if Aerodactyl/Dragonite are controlled or removed.
reflections.notebook: Opponent used the offensive Gengar/Aerodactyl/Dragonite/Arcanine mode in Game 1. Mega Gengar has shown a willingness to Protect when threatened by Scarf Garchomp. Aerodactyl is Focus Sash with Tailwind, Taunt, Wide Guard, and Rock Slide; respect it as the key disruption and Rock Slide source. Future plan: use Raichu to deny or slow Aerodactyl, and avoid relying on Mega Charizard Y while opposing Rock Slide pressure remains.
